name: Xevien Brinson
strengths: Brinson flexes wide as a big-slot / mismatch TE and creates vertical seams with 6-5 length over the second level.
Brinson finishes in space after the catch — long stride, ball security, and speed to punish light linebackers in the open field.
Brinson also attaches in-line in short yardage / goal-line — willing three-point work while keeping the mismatch receiving traits.
weaknesses: Brinson still needs functional mass at 6-5 / 210 before he can sustain every-down in-line work versus SEC edge setters.
comparison: Brinson comps to Mark Andrews — 6-5 athletic TE mold; flex alignments, seam length, and YAC who grows into a complete hybrid (size-matched; not a Florida-alum default).
projection: Brinson projects as earn package / mismatch snaps Year 1, compete for a starting hybrid TE role Year 2 — starter upside as a move/Y who wins with length and after-catch speed before the complete in-line base arrives.
schemeFit: Brinson fits a 12/11 TE room that values flexed mismatch snaps and growing in-line will as the frame fills.
